item.title: App Governance guidance: Last used policies cannot be created and existing evaluation is paused — 25 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 25 November 2026

App Governance guidance: Last used policies cannot be created and existing evaluation is paused

The period’s most consequential update concerns Cloud Apps App Governance: guidance now says policies using the Last used condition cannot be created, while existing policies using it are not evaluated. Those policies retain their configurations but generate no alerts or execute governance actions while evaluation is paused. Endpoint guidance also adds MDESupportTool signature verification and clarifies licensing for Windows Enterprise multi-session Azure Virtual Desktop users.

Cloud Apps · Cloud and workloads

App Governance limits the Last used condition

The guidance says administrators cannot create policies using Last used. Existing policies using that condition are not evaluated, so they do not generate alerts or execute governance actions; their configurations remain unchanged while evaluation is paused.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

MDESupportTool verification now requires signature and signer checks

The Run Analyzer Macos procedure instructs administrators to verify the MDESupportTool signature and Microsoft signer details with the provided codesign commands. It also updates the documented SHA-256 hash and renumbers the procedure. Do not run the tool if verification fails or the signer does not match.

Endpoint · Architecture and deployment

Multi-session Azure Virtual Desktop guidance adds an all-user licensing requirement

The onboarding guidance states that when Windows Enterprise multi-session is used with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, every Azure Virtual Desktop user accessing the virtual machines must have one of the listed licenses.

item.title: Copilot Studio real-time protection settings require action by December 23 — 24 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 24 November 2026

Copilot Studio real-time protection settings require action by December 23

All 19 entries were updates, but this was more than a mechanical reference-edit day. The most urgent guidance says the current Copilot Studio real-time-protection onboarding retires on December 2, blocking settings will not migrate automatically, and administrators must act by December 23, 2026 to keep protection enabled. Retention rules are the other major theme: XDR lists 30 days for AgentsInfo and IdentityAccountInfo, while Sentinel limits the stated 90-day inclusion to supported Microsoft Defender data and gives January 3, 2027 as the expected date for a full 90-day history. MDASH guidance also clarifies GPT-5.4 fallback behavior and MAI Cyber deployment constraints.

Defender XDR · General

Current Copilot Studio onboarding retires December 2

The updated guidance says the existing onboarding experience retires on December 2 and that its blocking settings will not migrate automatically. Administrators must take action by December 23, 2026 to keep real-time protection enabled for Copilot Studio agents.

Defender XDR · General

XDR guidance lists 30-day retention for two ISOC tables

The updated retention text says AgentsInfo and IdentityAccountInfo receive 30 days of retention in XDR rather than the 90-day included benefit. Extended retention starts at 180 days, and streaming supported Defender data starts the retention period at 180 days.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel guidance limits the stated 90-day retention scope

The table-retention guidance limits the stated 90-day included retention to supported Microsoft Defender data, notes source-dependent retention, marks several tables as Preview, and gives January 3, 2027 as the expected date for a full 90-day history. It also says additional charges apply based on ingestion and retention.

Exposure Management · Vulnerabilities and exposure

MDASH guidance specifies GPT-5.4 fallback and deployment limits

Codename MDASH automatically uses GPT-5.4 when GPT-5.3-Codex is unavailable. GPT-5.4 remains required, and this fallback does not cover runtime failures or throttling. MAI Cyber (Preview) must be deployed through Azure CLI and is limited to Global Standard deployments and supported regions.

Identity · Identity protection

Identity guidance flags risky non-admin password-reset rights

The Accounts guidance adds an assessment identifying non-admin accounts that can reset passwords for sensitive or privileged groups, with guidance to review and restrict those permissions. The permissions can enable privilege escalation and compromise of the Active Directory environment.

item.title: Custom detection rules gain preview alert grouping and richer entity mapping — 23 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 23 November 2026

Custom detection rules gain preview alert grouping and richer entity mapping

Defender XDR dominates the period: preview capabilities beginning November 17 describe grouping related alerts from the same rule into one incident and mapping repeated entity types with up to four identifier-and-column pairs per entity. The administrator path for alert grouping is now documented, while a separate correlation note says grouping occurs before Defender correlation and does not prevent later alert linking or incident merging. Outside XDR, Defender for Cloud reframed its Resource Manager detection scope, Office 365 added clearer quarantine inspection views, and Endpoint prerequisites now list Azure Linux 4.0.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

Custom detection alert grouping gets a preview configuration path

The manage page now documents preview alert grouping and directs administrators to Rule details > Edit > Incident settings > Alert grouping. It also links to the available configuration options and limits.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

Entity mappings add repeated types and four identifier pairs

The custom detection wizard now documents repeated entity types and up to four identifier-and-column pairs per entity. Newly supported identifiers are in preview, and mappings should be reviewed because identified entities affect incident correlation.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Resource Manager guidance centers on suspicious Azure control-plane activity

The Defender for Resource Manager article now presents threats detected in suspicious Azure control-plane activity through the Azure portal, REST APIs, CLI, and other programmatic clients, rather than an alert-by-alert catalog. Use the updated overview to understand the documented detection scope.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Quarantine review adds separate HTML and plain-text views

The quarantine instructions now provide Source and Plain text tabs. Source displays HTML with links disabled, while Plain text displays the message body without HTML formatting.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Azure Linux 4.0 appears in Defender for Endpoint prerequisites

The Linux prerequisites documentation now lists Azure Linux version 4.0, giving administrators an additional version to validate when assessing Linux deployments.

View all updates for 23 November 2026 →

item.title: AI agent blocking settings face a December 23 migration deadline — 22 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 22 November 2026

AI agent blocking settings face a December 23 migration deadline

The period’s main administrator concern is Defender XDR’s AI agent real-time protection transition: users of the existing onboarding path should migrate blocking settings by December 23, 2026, to keep real-time protection enabled. Sentinel’s custom-detection guidance now specifies automatic conversion of affected JSON columns when migrated rules run, while copied queries in Advanced Hunting still need `todynamic()` before accessing nested values. Defender XDR’s user-investigation guidance also adds a reset-identity-risk action.

Defender XDR · General

Existing AI-agent onboarding requires blocking-setting migration

The Defender XDR real-time protection page no longer includes the notice about blocking settings not migrating when the existing onboarding experience retires. Administrators using that path should migrate those settings by December 23, 2026 to keep real-time protection enabled.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Migrated Sentinel detections convert JSON columns at runtime

Migrated rules now automatically convert affected JSON columns when they run. Queries copied into Advanced Hunting still require `todynamic()` before administrators can access nested JSON values; documentation for two unavailable `ExtendedProperties` fields was also removed.

Defender XDR · General

Investigate Users guidance adds identity-risk reset action

The Defender XDR user-investigation page now states that administrators can reset an identity’s risk and links to the remediation-actions guidance for the procedure.

View all updates for 22 November 2026 →

item.title: AI prompt capture is unredacted while MDASH guidance adds code-finding validation — 21 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 21 November 2026

AI prompt capture is unredacted while MDASH guidance adds code-finding validation

The period’s substantive updates sharpen two administrator-facing areas. Exposure Management guidance describes the Run web pen test playbook using MDASH code-scanning findings to assess suspected code weaknesses, with lower token use, improved reliability, fewer duplicate findings, and a documented relaxation of the GPT-5.3-codex requirement. Endpoint guidance makes the data handling of AI agent prompt evidence collection explicit, while a related MDASH integration update adds an access-approval prerequisite for MAI Cyber (Preview).

Exposure Management · Vulnerabilities and exposure

Run web pen tests can assess suspected code weaknesses from MDASH findings

Updated Exposure Management guidance says the Run web pen test playbook can use MDASH code-scanning findings for validation. It also documents fewer-token scans, improved reliability, fewer duplicate findings, supported minimum model sets, and that GPT-5.3-codex is no longer mandatory.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Prompt evidence collection sends original prompts and tool calls to the cloud

Endpoint guidance states that enabling prompt evidence collection sends prompts and tool calls, including arguments, to the cloud in their original form. Captured content may appear in security alerts and is retained under the Microsoft Defender XDR data retention policy; sensitive content and secrets are not redacted.

Exposure Management · Vulnerabilities and exposure

MAI Cyber for MDASH requires an approved access request

The MDASH Foundry integration guidance states that using MAI Cyber (Preview) requires submitting an access request and receiving approval. Administrators must complete that process before using MAI Cyber for MDASH scans.

View all updates for 21 November 2026 →

item.title: Mdash Foundry guidance specifies three required models and Azure CLI for MAI Cyber — 20 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 20 November 2026

Mdash Foundry guidance specifies three required models and Azure CLI for MAI Cyber

The most actionable update is to Exposure Management’s Mdash Foundry integration guidance: three standard models must be deployed and verified before scans, while the optional recommended MAI-Cyber-1.1-Flash model requires one-time Azure CLI deployment and Global Standard. Defender XDR also documents four approved third-party synthetic-media detection engines, and Vulnerability Management records corrections to recommendations, detections, and end-of-support details.

Exposure Management · Vulnerabilities and exposure

Mdash Foundry adds explicit model prerequisites and MAI Cyber deployment steps

The Exposure Management integration page now specifies three required standard models and the optional recommended MAI-Cyber-1.1-Flash configuration. It adds Azure CLI deployment instructions and identifies Global Standard as MAI Cyber’s supported deployment type. The three standard models must be deployed and verified before scans; MAI Cyber must be deployed once through Azure CLI because portal deployment is not supported.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

Defender XDR names four approved third-party synthetic-media detection engines

Advanced Hunting documentation now lists GetReal, Pindrop, Reality Defender, and Resemble AI alongside Microsoft as approved engines for synthetic-media detection event data.

Vulnerability Management · General

Vulnerability Management corrects recommendations and expands detection coverage

The updated page records corrected vulnerability recommendations, improved Zoom Workplace and Zabbix Agent detection, expanded support for Microsoft JDBC Driver and Process Monitor, and revised end-of-support details for selected products. Administrators should review the affected recommendations, detections, and lifecycle information.

View all updates for 20 November 2026 →

item.title: AI agent real-time protection settings face a December 23 migration deadline — 19 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 19 November 2026

AI agent real-time protection settings face a December 23 migration deadline

Administrators using the existing AI agent onboarding experience must complete the documented steps by December 23, 2026, because blocking settings will not migrate when that experience ends on December 2. Runtime-protection guidance also warns that alert prompt snippets are unredacted and may contain conversations, sensitive data, and secrets. Separately, Defender for Cloud Apps is preparing App Governance permission changes for selected Entra roles in December 2026; Defender for Containers guidance requires Linux kernel 5.15 or later for the latest sensor capabilities; and Defender for Identity v3.x activation without Defender for Endpoint is now allowed in government clouds. The remaining updates are mainly hunting-schema, coverage-label, terminology, and integration-prerequisite clarifications, including Azure region and Azure OpenAI Responses API requirements for AI Code Security.

Defender XDR · General

Existing AI agent onboarding has a blocking-settings deadline

Administrators using the existing onboarding experience must complete the documented steps by December 23, 2026. The experience ends December 2, and its blocking settings will not migrate; completing the steps preserves real-time protection.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Runtime-protection alerts may expose unredacted prompt content

Configuration guidance now warns that prompt snippets shown in alerts are not redacted and may contain conversations, sensitive data, and secrets. Administrators should account for that exposure when reviewing or sharing alerts.

Defender XDR · General

App Governance permissions shift for selected Entra roles

The December 2026 Defender for Cloud Apps rollout adds policy-management rights to Cloud App Security Administrators and removes some permissions from Compliance Administrators and Compliance Data Administrators with Unified RBAC support. Review and update role assignments accordingly.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Defender for Containers support splits at Linux kernel 5.15

The support matrix states that the latest Defender sensor capabilities require Linux Kernel 5.15 or later. Kernel 5.4 or later supports limited functionality, so clusters on 5.4 through 5.14 may not receive the latest capabilities.

Identity · Identity protection

Government clouds can activate Defender for Identity v3.x independently

Updated guidance resolves the previous limitation on activating Defender for Identity Sensor v3.x without Defender for Endpoint in government cloud environments.

View all updates for 19 November 2026 →

item.title: App Governance previews delegated NHI RBAC as classic identity alerts retire this month — 18 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 18 November 2026

App Governance previews delegated NHI RBAC as classic identity alerts retire this month

Two changes carry the greatest operational weight: App Governance is scheduled to add unified Defender XDR RBAC for Non-Human Identity management in public preview from late November, while two classic Defender for Identity alerts are scheduled to retire at month-end. Defender for IoT guidance now uses August 15, 2027, instead of June 1, 2027, for the planned micro agent retirement. Most other updates refresh terminology, navigation, metadata, or references, with useful clarifications for Endpoint Performance mode and the Purview connector name.

Defender XDR · General

Unified Defender XDR RBAC is coming to App Governance

Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps App Governance will support unified Defender XDR RBAC in public preview starting in late November 2026. Administrators will be able to assign custom roles for Non-Human Identity viewing, policy management, and service management, with rollout scheduled to complete by mid-January 2027.

Identity · Identity protection

Two classic identity alerts are scheduled for month-end retirement

The Suspected identity theft (pass-the-hash) and Remote code execution attempt classic alerts are scheduled to retire at the end of November 2026. The guidance points administrators to Defender for Endpoint behavioral blocking and containment, plus custom detections in Advanced hunting, as monitoring alternatives.

IoT · General

Defender for IoT guidance moves the planned micro agent retirement date

The documented planned retirement date for the Defender for IoT micro agent changed from June 1, 2027, to August 15, 2027. Administrators should use the revised date for deployment and lifecycle planning.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Performance mode guidance separates PowerShell and Intune status values

The Endpoint guidance now states that Get-MpPreference reports PerformanceModeStatus as 1 when enabled and 0 when disabled, opposite to the values used in Intune. It also directs administrators to See volumes in Windows Security to check a volume’s status.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

The Purview connector setup guidance drops the Preview label

The Sentinel setup page now names the connector Microsoft Purview Information Protection instead of Microsoft Purview Information Protection (Preview) and removes the preview notice. Administrators should use the revised connector name when following the instructions.

View all updates for 18 November 2026 →

item.title: Sentinel ISOC preview details tenant transition and analytics-rule migration paths — 17 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 17 November 2026

Sentinel ISOC preview details tenant transition and analytics-rule migration paths

The period’s consequential Sentinel changes are new guidance for the preview Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC): existing deployments can transition under an irreversible tenant-wide scope, and eligible analytics rules can be converted to Defender custom detections and validated before cutover. Other material updates cover promotional-mail handling in Defender for Office 365, Defender for Servers billing rules, and the deprecation of Defender for Endpoint support for Amazon Linux 2 ARM64. Much of the remaining update set is lower-impact Identity terminology and portal-navigation cleanup, including revised Sensor Management paths.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

ISOC transition guidance sets an irreversible tenant-wide scope

New Microsoft Sentinel guidance identifies ISOC as a preview capability and explains how existing deployments opt in. It calls for eligibility and permission checks, connection of all workspaces, and review of changed discounts, pricing, and data benefits; the transition is described as irreversible at tenant scope.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

SOC optimization migration converts eligible analytics rules into custom detections

The new migration procedure explains how to convert eligible Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules into Microsoft Defender custom detections, validate the results, and complete migration. Original rules remain enabled during evaluation and should be disabled only after alert behavior and dependent automation have been checked.

Defender XDR · Email and collaboration

Defender for Office 365 rollout adds promotional-mail tagging and folder handling

A Microsoft 365 Message Center major update says promotional messages will be tagged as “promotions” and can be moved automatically to a Promotions folder, with the system learning from user actions. The notice lists public preview beginning in mid-April 2026 and general rollout beginning in late July 2026; administrators control the settings.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Defender for Servers billing rules account for protection and power state

The updated Defender for Servers FAQ states that from November 1, 2026, machines are billed only when protected by Plan 1 or Plan 2 and in a billable power state. Plan 1 billing also distinguishes desktop devices from servers using operating-system and device information, with updated agent and classification rules.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Defender for Endpoint deprecates Amazon Linux 2 ARM64 support

The Linux prerequisites guidance states that Defender for Endpoint support for Amazon Linux 2 on ARM64 was deprecated on October 31, 2026, and removes the previous last-version and support-end details.

View all updates for 17 November 2026 →

item.description:
Day in brief · 14 November 2026

Defender for Endpoint adds individual controls for public-preview features

This was a documentation-led period, but several updates carry direct administrator consequences. Defender for Endpoint now documents a portal page for enabling or disabling selected public-preview features tenant-wide or through a safe deployment channel. Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Selected public previews can be managed by tenant or safe deployment channel

A new Defender for Endpoint portal page lets administrators enable or disable selected public-preview features tenant-wide or by safe deployment channel. Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Exchange Security Insights guidance requires Log Monitor API migration

The on-premises and online Exchange Security Insights collectors are marked for migration to Azure Monitor, with the documented update changing from the Azure Log Analytics HTTP Data Collector API to the Log Monitor API. Administrators are advised to update the collector to version 8.0.0.0 or later.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Offboarding deployment tools can carry a portal-generated key

The deployment-tool procedure supports a Defender portal offboarding key with configurable expiration and interactive or quiet command-line offboarding; the existing .offboarding-file method remains available. The key cannot be viewed again and works only with the tool that generated it.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel data lake retention now requires a supported workspace region

The retention guidance states that a workspace must be in a supported region to use data lake retention.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

ASIM references separate parser timing and clarify packed unmapped fields

The ASIM reference now distinguishes query-time and ingestion-time parsers, links to parser definitions, and clarifies that pack=true retains unmapped fields in AdditionalFields. It also adds native normalized entries and additional data sources.

item.description:

item.title: Multi-recipient Defender for Office 365 policies switch to OR matching when modified — 10 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 10 November 2026

Multi-recipient Defender for Office 365 policies switch to OR matching when modified

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is scheduled to change multi-recipient threat-policy inclusion from Match all (AND) to Match any (OR) in December 2026 when an affected policy is modified. That can expand policy scope, while existing policies are not automatically converted. Other substantive guidance covers a 100 MiB limit for portal retrieval of quarantined files, verdict enforcement for certain quarantined mail, preview-scoped Azure security tasks in the Defender portal, and consolidated Sentinel connector-health monitoring. Most remaining updates refine terminology, headings, links, metadata, and navigation across Defender XDR and Identity.

Defender XDR · General

Recipient matching changes from Match all to Match any on policy modification

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is scheduled to interpret multiple specified recipient types with Match any (OR), instead of Match all (AND), when a threat-protection policy is modified in December 2026. Existing policies are not auto-converted, but modifying one can expand its scope.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Endpoint guidance limits portal downloads to cloud-backed files up to 100 MiB

The updated Respond File Alerts guidance says portal downloads use a cloud-backed copy rather than the device’s local quarantine. Cloud backup covers files up to 100 MiB; larger files remain quarantined but cannot be downloaded from the portal. Collect file retrieves the current device path and may fail if quarantine removed the original.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Quarantined malware and high-confidence phishing verdicts cannot be bypassed on release

When MX points to Microsoft 365, the updated guidance says malware and high-confidence phishing messages quarantined under that setup cannot bypass their verdict when released. Administrators must resolve the verdict before release.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Azure Defender portal comparison adds four preview-scoped security tasks

The updated comparison lists Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark, security policies, exemptions, and regulatory compliance assessments as available in preview for Azure environments in the Defender portal.

Sentinel · Developer and API

Sentinel guidance consolidates connector-health checks in Data & connectors

The updated guidance describes the Defender portal’s Data & connectors Overview tab for reviewing connector counts, ingestion volume and growth, errors, table fluctuations, and ingestion latency, with links to connector and table details.

item.description:

Unified RBAC guidance now requires both Defender for Office 365 and Exchange Online toggles

The supplied period is documentation-led, with the strongest administrator impact concentrated in RBAC prerequisites and Microsoft Sentinel operating procedures. Multiple Office 365 policy articles now state that both the Defender for Office 365 and Exchange Online permissions toggles under Email & collaboration must be Active for the documented Unified RBAC scenarios. Office 365 policy guidance standardizes a two-toggle Unified RBAC prerequisite

The guidance now covers connector and table management, transformations, and ingestion-health monitoring in the unified Defender portal through Overview, Connectors, and Tables tabs. The article distinguishes Microsoft Defender SOC Logic Apps and generated playbooks from Sentinel connector Logic Apps. item.description:
Day in brief · 20 October 2026

Defender portal preview brings Azure plan management, DWU billing, and server onboarding

Defender for Cloud is the clear center of gravity: new and revised guidance describes a preview for connecting Azure commercial subscriptions or management groups, managing cloud security plans in the Defender portal, and estimating costs with Defender Workload Units (DWUs). Supporting updates clarify tenant-wide server onboarding, broaden Defender for Identity sensor v3.x coverage, and flag an upcoming Defender for Cloud Apps permission change.

Defender for Cloud plan management moves into a scoped portal preview

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

DWU guidance adds cost estimation and post-adoption reporting

Direct onboarding is explicitly tenant-wide for eligible non-Azure servers

The updated procedure states that Direct onboarding affects all eligible existing and future non-Azure servers in the same Microsoft Entra tenant; individual-server or pilot-group selection is unsupported. Administrators must verify healthy Defender for Endpoint telemetry, a matching tenant, and the required roles before enabling it.

Identity · Architecture and deployment

Updated guidance documents sensor v3.x onboarding with or without Defender for Endpoint for eligible Windows Server 2019 or later AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers, extending the documented coverage beyond domain controllers.

Defender XDR · General

App Governance permissions will change for three Entra roles

Starting in mid-November 2026, Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps will align App Governance role-based access with Defender XDR. The change affects the Cloud App Security, Compliance Administrator, and Compliance Data Administrator roles, so administrators should review and update role assignments.

item.title: Defender for Identity sensor v3 guidance shifts to September cumulative updates — 14 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 14 October 2026

Defender for Identity sensor v3 guidance shifts to September cumulative updates

This was primarily a documentation-maintenance day—22 updates and one removed page, with no new entries—but several changes have direct operational consequences. Defender for Identity guidance now centers on September 2026 Windows Server updates and clarifies sensor migration and offboarding behavior. Defender for Cloud documents an AWS scan-suspension threshold, while Defender XDR clarifies both the AIAgentsInfo-to-AgentsInfo schema transition and where DLP signals can be investigated.

Identity · Architecture and deployment

Defender for Identity sensor v3 prerequisites move to September 2026 cumulative updates

The Deploy Sensor V3 guidance replaces the July 2026 prerequisite with the September 2026 Windows Server cumulative update for sensor version 3.0.10 or later. It also clarifies that administrators should select the local system account option before v2 migration and that migration does not automatically remove workspace DSA or gMSA configuration.

Identity · Identity protection

Defender for Identity guidance separates Endpoint offboarding from identity-only operation

The FAQ states that offboarding a server from Defender for Endpoint stops Defender for Identity v3.x sensor reporting, including sensors migrated from v2.x, and does not automatically enable identity-only mode. Deployments needing identity-only protection should use the onboarding method that excludes Defender for Endpoint.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

AWS agentless scanning suspends new scans after 250 failed-deletion snapshots

Defender for Cloud guidance says that 250 or more Defender-tagged snapshots accumulated because of deletion authorization failures suspend new scans for the affected AWS scope. The snapshots continue accruing storage charges until deleted, so administrators should verify ec2:DeleteSnapshot authorization and review AWS policy restrictions.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

Advanced hunting transitions agent data from AIAgentsInfo to AgentsInfo

The AIAgentsInfo reference was removed as the schema transitions to unified AgentsInfo, which expands beyond Copilot Studio-specific columns. The removed reference states that AIAgentsInfo remains accessible until July 1, 2026; affected queries should be updated to AgentsInfo.

Defender XDR · General

DLP signals remain in advanced hunting rather than the incident queue

The guidance says the built-in rule took effect in early October 2026, but DLP signals are treated as behaviors: they do not generate alerts or appear in the incident queue and remain available in advanced hunting. Investigators should use advanced hunting for these signals.

item.description:
Day in brief · 13 October 2026

Defender XDR guidance details explicit per-rule controls for custom detections

The period is dominated by documentation maintenance, but four updates carry useful operational detail. Separate guidance covers July 2026 bulk-mail routing, Azure CSPM prerequisites for recommendation exemptions, and Defender for Containers provisioning failures.

Custom detections have documented per-rule correlation controls

The updated Defender XDR guidance states that custom detections are included in correlation by default and can be included or excluded on a per-rule basis. The Office 365 anti-spam guidance says that, as of July 2026, messages identified as bulk receive the Promotions tag. When Bulk moves enabled is turned on, messages move from Inbox to the Promotions folder only when they are promotional in nature, regardless of BCL value.

Defender for Cloud · Identity protection

Azure CSPM assignment controls exemptions for some recommendations

Defender for Cloud guidance now explains that some identity and access recommendations can appear without the Azure CSPM standard assigned, but those recommendations do not support exemptions unless the standard is assigned. Administrators needing exemptions should assign the standard and follow the linked assignment procedure.

Defender for Cloud · Troubleshooting

Defender for Containers adds EKS and Azure Arc troubleshooting paths

The troubleshooting guidance now covers EKS provisioning failures caused by recreated IAM roles, endpoint allowlist reconciliation, and stale Azure Arc registrations. It adds diagnostic commands and resolution steps, including preserving required Defender provisioning network ranges in infrastructure automation.

Identity activation is limited to new sensor v3.x deployments

The new ASIM reference defines email routing, authentication, delivery-outcome, and threat fields, and documents the `_Im_EmailEvent` parser, custom parser naming, and filtering parameters. item.title: Custom detections spell out 5-minute-to-14-day scheduling and lookback boundaries — 4 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 4 October 2026

Custom detections spell out 5-minute-to-14-day scheduling and lookback boundaries

The period focuses on guidance changes that sharpen administrator decisions. Custom-detection pages spell out the 5-minute-to-14-day custom-frequency range, the Sentinel-only data-source boundary, fixed 4-hour-to-30-day lookbacks for Defender XDR data, and Sentinel lookback limits that remain in public preview. Other meaningful updates clarify Unified RBAC coverage for identity exclusions, restrict two Cloud Apps admin roles in new configurations, and record four GA Defender for Cloud sensor builds with security and dependency fixes.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

Custom frequency is restricted to Sentinel-only detections

Updated Custom Detection Rules guidance says custom frequency from 5 minutes to 14 days is available only for rules based exclusively on Microsoft Sentinel data. Rules using Defender XDR data instead use fixed lookback periods tied to run frequency, ranging from 4 hours to 30 days, and cannot use custom scoping with this frequency option.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel guidance sets preview lookback ceilings by frequency

The comparison guidance lists flexible and high-frequency support for Sentinel data: lookback is up to 48 hours when frequency exceeds one hour and up to 14 days when frequency is one hour or less. Lookback remains labeled public preview.

Defender XDR · General

Identity-exclusion guidance covers both response products

The updated guidance explains that identity exclusions affect automated response actions in both Defender for Identity and Defender for Endpoint. Its Unified RBAC permissions coverage now addresses both products’ data sources, role assignments, and data-source scope.

Cloud Apps · Cloud and workloads

Cloud Apps admin roles are unavailable for new configurations

App/instance admin and User group admin role assignments can no longer be used in new configurations. Existing configurations remain supported, and organizations needing these capabilities are directed to Microsoft Support.

Defender for Cloud · Identity protection

Defender for Cloud records four September GA sensor builds

The sensor changelog now lists versions 0.11.7, 0.10.10, 0.9.68, and 0.8.61 as September 2026 GA releases, each containing security vulnerability fixes and dependency updates.

item.title: Defender for Office 365 rolls out promotional-mail tagging and automatic folder moves — 2 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 2 October 2026

Defender for Office 365 rolls out promotional-mail tagging and automatic folder moves

Defender for Office 365 will label promotional emails as “promotions” and can move them automatically to a Promotions folder, learning from user actions. Separately, the Office 365 permissions documentation removes the “related to Copilot” qualifier from descriptions of Data Security AI Admin DLP permissions while retaining the exclusion for prompt and response access.

Defender XDR · Email and collaboration

Promotional emails gain “promotions” labels and automatic folder handling

Microsoft says Defender for Office 365 will tag promotional emails as “promotions” and can automatically move them to a Promotions folder. The capability learns from user actions, and users can customize handling by moving messages. Public preview starts in mid-April 2026, with general rollout completing by late 2026.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Data Security AI Admin descriptions remove the Copilot qualifier

The Scc Permissions page now describes Data Security AI Admins and the Data Security AI Admin role as able to edit Data Loss Prevention policies without the previous “related to Copilot” qualifier. It continues to document access to view AI content, while prompt and response access remains excluded.
